title: Trump Declares Himself 'Guardian of the Hormuz Strait' and Demands 20% Toll. Kpler Data Shows 14 Vessels Transit — Down 90% From Pre-War Levels.
narrative:
President Trump declared on July 13 that the United States will become "THE GUARDIAN OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT" and charge a 20% toll on all cargo shipped through the waterway, claiming the strait is "open" and will remain so "with or without Iran." Trump told Fox News: "We're going to keep the strait, and we'll probably run it. We'll become the guardian of the strait. Maybe we'll call it the 'Guardian Angel of the Strait.' And we should be reimbursed for that." On Truth Social, he wrote: "The U.S.A. will be, from this point forward, known as 'THE GUARDIAN OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT,' but as such, and as a matter of FAIRNESS, will be reimbursed, at the rate of 20% on all cargo shipped." He also announced reinstatement of "THE IRANIAN BLOCKADE" — stopping only Iranian ships and their customers. CENTCOM maintained the strait is "open to all vessels seeking to lawfully transit."

The commercial reality directly contradicts the "open strait" characterization. Kpler shipping data shows only 14 commercial vessels transited Hormuz on Sunday July 12 — a 60% decline from 37 vessels the same day the previous week. Before the war began February 28, an average of 130 vessels crossed daily. After the June 14 MoU, traffic recovered to approximately 70 daily crossings. The 14-vessel figure is near the war's lowest point. Windward maritime intelligence analysts stated the southern route protected by the US military "has effectively collapsed." Kpler confirmed traffic through the Omani corridor "had all but disappeared over the weekend." MarineTraffic.com reported traffic "dropped to minimal levels, indicating that operators continue to prioritize perceived security over more direct transit options."

The vessels that did transit on Sunday included the Humanity (2 million barrels Iranian crude), Burg Star (500,000 barrels dirty petroleum products), Capetan Andreas (500,000 barrels dirty petroleum products from Kuwait), and Minoan Courage (fertilizer from Saudi Arabia to India). Most other ships were sailing without cargo — ballast transits, not commercial flows. Iran fired warning shots at two ships attempting to transit without authorization and struck a commercial vessel on Sunday whose crew abandoned ship in a lifeboat east of Oman. The IRGC declared the strait closed "until further notice."
analysis:
The structural finding is that Trump's "open strait, we guard it, you pay us" narrative describes a strait that is commercially non-functional. The 14-vessel transit count — versus 130 pre-war and 70 post-MoU — means the 20% toll would apply to a flow that is 90% below normal. The toll is a tax on a phantom revenue base: it generates money only if traffic recovers, but traffic cannot recover while the United States and Iran are actively shooting at commercial vessels. The southern route's "effective collapse" means the US-protected alternative that was supposed to be the basis for "open" transit has itself become the danger zone.

The parallel between Trump condemning Iran's "fees" for strait passage weeks earlier and then proposing his own 20% cargo charge is a direct on-record contradiction within a three-week window. The US had accused Iran of extortion for suggesting commercial ships pay for safe passage; Trump now proposes the identical mechanism under the branding of "reimbursement." The Kpler data is the physical evidence that makes the political claim unfalsifiable in the wrong direction — it is not that the strait is "open" or "closed," it is that it is commercially dead, and the toll is a policy proposal applied to a corpse.

The 2 million barrels on the Humanity and the 500,000-barrel cargoes on Burg Star and Capetan Andreas represent the actual commercial activity the toll would capture: Iranian crude transiting under IRGC protection, Kuwaiti petroleum products moving through a war zone, and Saudi fertilizer bound for India. The toll's economic logic depends on traffic volume that no longer exists, while the security logic depends on a protective umbrella that has itself become a target. The 14-vessel count is not a temporary dip — it is the structural floor of a waterway where both sides are actively engaging commercial traffic as a instrument of coercion.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: Trump's 20% toll proposal applies to a waterway carrying 14 vessels per day — down 90% from pre-war levels and 80% from the post-MoU recovery. The commercial reality has collapsed faster than the political narrative can describe it: Kpler data shows the southern US-protected route has "effectively collapsed," the IRGC has declared the strait closed "until further notice," and the actual vessels transiting are mostly ballast runs and Iranian crude moving under IRGC escort. The toll mirrors the exact fee structure Trump condemned when Iran proposed it three weeks earlier — a direct on-record contradiction in a 3-week window, applied to a waterway that no longer functions as a commercial transit route.
